    <h1>Exploring the Relationship Between Sleep Duration and College GPA</h1>
    <p>A statistical analysis examining whether college students’ average sleep duration is associated with semester GPA.</p>

  <section class="poster-section">

    <div class="question-text">
      Is there an association between average sleep duration and academic performance among college students?
    </div>

  <!-- METHODOLOGY -->
  <section class="poster-section">
    <div class="section-heading">
      <img src="../../assets/logo.png" alt="">
      <span>Methodology</span>
      <img src="../../assets/logo.png" alt="">
    </div>

    <div class="section-text method-text">
      <p>
        The analysis uses data from students at Carnegie Mellon University and two other universities, where students wore sleep trackers for one month during the spring semester. A simple linear regression was implemented in R to evaluate the association between sleep duration and academic performance. Based on exploratory data analysis, the model focused on students’ average nightly sleep time and semester GPA.
      </p>
      <ul>
        <li><strong>Simple Linear Regression:</strong> Models the association between TotalSleepTime and term_gpa.</li>
        <li><strong>Variable Transformation:</strong> TotalSleepTime was converted from minutes to hours (divided by 60), so the slope is the average GPA difference per additional hour of sleep.</li>
        <li><strong>Model Evaluation:</strong> The regression plot suggested a plausibly linear relationship, though visible variation around the fitted line indicated the model may not capture all patterns.</li>
      </ul>
    </div>
  </section>

  <!-- MODEL RESULTS -->
  <section class="poster-section">
    <div class="section-heading">
      <img src="../../assets/logo.png" alt="">
      <span>Model Results</span>
      <img src="../../assets/logo.png" alt="">
    </div>

    <div class="stat-row">
      <div class="stat">
        <div class="stat-number">0.1191</div>
        <p>Estimated GPA increase associated with one additional hour of sleep.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="stat">
        <div class="stat-number">3.04 × 10<sup>−7</sup></div>
        <p>P-value for the sleep duration coefficient, indicating statistical significance.</p>
      </div>
    </div>

    <div class="split results-split">
      <div class="plot">
        <img src="plot1-401.png" alt="Scatterplot of sleep duration and semester GPA with fitted regression line">
      </div>

      <div class="section-text">
        <p>
          The fitted model found a positive slope estimate for sleep duration. The p-value was very small, providing evidence that the slope coefficient is not equal to zero.
        </p>
      </div>
    </div>
  </section>

  <!-- KEY FINDINGS -->
